model.name: cafe-service
model.description: Variation II — the café as an operations what-if model, in the vocabulary sim.pflow.xyz calibrates and diagnoses. Every service is two firings (start_brew seizes a barista and the machine, finish_brew and hand_over release them) so headcount is observably busy. Queue -> start arcs are kinetic:false with a 720/h pickup: a free barista does not notice a waiting customer faster because more are waiting; the declared service time lives on finish_brew, which is Erlang-3 (stages: 3) because a shot takes about as long every time. Demand carries its own day shape (schedule on arrive: dead open, rush, quiet afternoon). The queue has capacity 8 (arrivals balk when it is full) and waiting customers give up at 3/h each (kinetic patience). VIPs arrive through their own source, rate 0 until a scenario raises it, and inhibit routine starts so they take the next free barista. The Open sign is a read arc. Restock is inhibited while beans >= 40. shot_size is a declared parameter binding both bean arcs, so a scenario cannot change one without the other. The objective nets served drinks against walkouts and idle barista-hours.

transitions.description: customers arriving; declared day shape — dead open, mid-morning rush, quiet afternoon
a waiting customer leaves without ordering (patience, ~20 min)
a free barista takes the next customer to the machine (pickup, ~5 s)
the shot is pulled (~3 min, Erlang-3: predictable)
drink handed over, barista back on the floor (~1 min)
VIPs arriving; rate 0 in the base model (see simulation.solver.rates) until a scenario raises it
a free barista makes the VIP drink at the bar (~4 min, no machine)
bean delivery of 40 shots (~every 30 min when allowed); inhibited while the hopper holds 40 or more
meter: one idle barista-hour per free barista per hour

parameters.description: bean shots per drink; binds the routine and VIP bean arcs so a scenario moves both

assumptions: transitions declaring neither stages nor a delay draw exponential durations — the most erratic a step can be for a given average. Staged transitions are the exception: finish_brew (Erlang-3) draw phase-type durations with the declared lower spread, so their waiting reflects the declaration rather than the worst case.

assumptions: transitions declaring neither stages nor a delay draw exponential durations — the most erratic a step can be for a given average. Staged transitions are the exception: finish_brew (Erlang-3) draw phase-type durations with the declared lower spread, so their waiting reflects the declaration rather than the worst case.

this engine assumes every step takes a random, exponentially distributed amount of time, which is the most erratic a shop can be for a given average. Work with a predictable duration — a shot pulls in about the same time every time — queues roughly half as much, so treat the waiting and the walkouts here as the bad case, not the typical one.
